title: FAA grounds HPE Juniper routers after outage halted US flights
byline: Giacomo Lee This article originally appeared
html:
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has suspended installation of Juniper network routers across its network after flights were grounded across the US last week, with Juniper parent Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) stressing the issue is configuration-based.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy announced the decision on Tuesday (November 17), telling the press that the migration from Cisco to Juniper kit had gone hitch-free for a year. Things, though, changed after the successful testing and installation of 68 routers to date, with Duffy commenting that "this was the 69th, and 68 had gone really well. This was the one that started to behave this way. So we thought it's only prudent to pause the use of these routers."

Duffy was referring to the rogue router, which was said to have caused Friday's outage, which resulted in more than 17,000 cancelled flights in the longest grounding of flights since the 9/11 terrorist attacks in 2001. Weekend reports claimed the device was undergoing tests at a Florida lab belonging to L3Harris Technologies, the defense contractor currently transforming the legacy copper network behind the FAA Telecommunications Infrastructure (FTI) to fiber-optic connectivity.

CRN reported that those tests have yet to determine whether the hardware was the smoking gun behind the last nationwide ground stop, and that the equipment was actually a copper-to-fiber media converter. The detail came from an unnamed source, who added that the broadcasting feature on the router should have been switched off during activation because it was communicating with a large network of 20-year-old Cisco 600 Series routers, thus crashing the system.

The FAA pause came on the same day Democrat lawmakers pressed Duffy to suspend Juniper installations.

In response to this title's request for comment, HPE pointed to previous remarks it made to the media, stressing that the device functioned as it was configured by the installer and did not fail or act improperly.
summary: Network modernization paused following Democrat calls
